prompt:
I need you to analyze screenshots of my personal portfolio website. I've already shared screenshots with you in a previous message. Please provide:

1. A detailed description of the current state of the website
2. All problems/issues you notice (visual glitches, alignment issues, responsiveness, UX problems, etc.)
3. Step-by-step instructions for fixing each problem

If you can't see the screenshots from the previous message, please let me know and I can re-upload them.
response:
Complete Portfolio Website Review

I've examined the full-page screenshot you shared earlier, including the enlarged views of its individual sections. This review covers the navigation, hero, Engineering Network, Home Security System, five interactive engineering demonstrations, contact section, and the overall visual design.

I'll focus on three things for each area: what currently exists, what looks wrong or underdeveloped, and exactly how your coding agent should approach fixing it.

Overall assessment: The website has a coherent technical theme and a promising collection of engineering interactions. However, its current presentation is considerably closer to a functional prototype than the immersive, visually distinctive engineering portfolio described in your original plan.

The primary problems are structural rather than cosmetic: excessive unused space, a disconnected Engineering Network, an undersized flagship architecture, inconsistent visual hierarchy, and engineering demonstrations that look like isolated widgets rather than connected parts of one portfolio experience.

These problems should be addressed through deliberate layout and component improvements, not by adding more decorative animations.

One limitation: I can assess what is visible in the screenshots, but I cannot establish whether animations, mobile layouts, keyboard controls, or navigation work correctly without seeing those states in a browser. I will distinguish visible problems from functionality that still needs testing.

PART 1 — Overall website design
1. Current state

The website uses a predominantly black and charcoal color scheme with white typography and restrained electrical signal colors.

The homepage is organized into a sequence of full-width sections:

Navigation + Hero

Personal identity and introductory statement

Engineering Network

Signal trace and engineering-domain nodes

Home Security Embedded System

Vertical system architecture

Interactive engineering demonstrations

Ultrasonic → Joystick → FPGA → ARM → Power

Contact

Open Circuit? + contact CTA

The design uses minimal borders, small technical labels, centered section headings, and compact instrumentation panels.

There is a consistent engineering-inspired aesthetic, but the individual sections do not yet form a convincing continuous visual experience.

2. Problem: Excessive empty space

This is the most noticeable issue across the entire screenshot.

The hero has a large empty area on the right. The Engineering Network uses very little of its available space. The Home Security System occupies a narrow central column, while the interactive demonstrations are comparatively small and surrounded by large margins.

Empty space can give a design a premium appearance, but it needs to support the composition.

Here, the space often appears unused rather than intentional.

Fix instructions

Establish one consistent maximum content width for the entire homepage.

Use a shared container for the hero, Engineering Network, architecture, and interactive demonstrations.

Create layouts that use the available horizontal space according to the content. Do not automatically center every section inside a narrow column.

Give the flagship project a substantially larger visual footprint than the smaller demonstrations.

Audit every section for unused space caused by unnecessary min-height, fixed heights, oversized padding, or narrow max-width values.

Remove unnecessary space rather than filling it with decorative graphics.

A reasonable initial container implementation is:

CSS
.page-container {
  width: min(100% - 64px, 1440px);
  margin-inline: auto;
}

@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .page-container {
    width: calc(100% - 32px);
  }
}

Treat these values as a starting point. The final widths should be determined through actual browser screenshots.

3. Problem: Weak visual hierarchy between major sections

The Home Security System is supposed to be the flagship project, but it receives approximately the same visual treatment as the smaller demonstrations.

The visitor is not given a clear distinction between your most substantial engineering work and your smaller experiments.

Fix instructions

Establish three levels of visual hierarchy.

Primary

Flagship project

Large typography, substantial visual area, detailed system architecture, prominent project navigation, and immersive interaction.

Secondary

Selected engineering work

Medium-sized interactive previews, concise explanations, and direct links to complete case studies.

Supporting

Technical metadata

Small monospace labels, instrumentation details, and supplementary information.

Apply this hierarchy consistently throughout the homepage.

The flagship architecture should command attention immediately, while the smaller demonstrations should support the broader engineering narrative.

4. Problem: Text contrast and readability

Many small labels, descriptions, and instrument readings appear extremely faint.

Some technical metadata seems to rely on very dark gray text against nearly black backgrounds.

The compressed screenshot makes this worse, so the exact readability needs to be confirmed at the original viewport resolution.

Nevertheless, the visual hierarchy relies too heavily on dimming secondary content.

Fix instructions

Inspect actual computed text colors and font sizes in the browser.

Establish consistent design tokens for primary, secondary, and tertiary text.

Use high-contrast text for information required to understand the engineering demonstrations.

Reserve subdued colors for genuinely supplementary information.

Keep technical labels small only when their role justifies it.

Ensure interactive measurements remain readable without zooming.

Check contrast against WCAG requirements.

Suggested starting tokens:

CSS
:root {
  --color-bg: #080a0a;
  --color-surface: #111414;

  --color-text-primary: #e9ece6;
  --color-text-secondary: #b2bab5;
  --color-text-tertiary: #8b9290;

  --color-signal: #b6ff4a;
  --color-logic: #6edcff;
  --color-power: #ffb547;
}

Do not fix readability by indiscriminately increasing the opacity of every element.

Different text roles should remain visually distinct.

PART 2 — Navigation
Current state

The navigation uses a small personal logo on the left, four primary navigation links around the center, and a green availability indicator on the right.

It is compact and restrained.

The layout is appropriate for a minimal portfolio, but it does not yet have a strong connection to the rest of the site's visual language.
